function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

**Paris** – the capital city of France – is one of the world’s most iconic urban centers, known for its rich history, art, fashion, cuisine, and cultural influence. | Topic | Highlights | |-------|------------| | **Location & Geography** | Situated in northern France along the Seine River, Paris covers roughly 105 km² (40 sq mi). The city is divided into 20 arrondissements (districts) that spiral clockwise from the center. | | **Population** | About 2.1 million residents live within the city limits (as of 2023), while the greater metropolitan area (Île‑de‑France) houses ~12 million people. | | **History** | • Founded as a Gallo‑Roman settlement (Lutetia) in the 3rd century BC.
• Became the capital of the Kingdom of France in the 14th century.
• Site of major events: French Revolution, World Wars, and the 1968 student protests. | | **Landmarks & Attractions** | • **Eiffel Tower** – 330 m iron lattice tower built for the 1889 Exposition Universelle.
• **Notre‑Dame de Paris** – Gothic cathedral (currently under restoration after the 2019 fire).
• **Louvre Museum** – world's largest art museum; home to the Mona Lisa and Venus de Milo.
• **Arc de Triomphe** – monument honoring those who fought for France.
• **Palace of Versailles** – opulent royal residence just outside Paris.
• **Montmartre** – historic bohemian district with Sacré‑Coeur Basilica. | | **Culture & Arts** | • Renowned for fashion weeks (Paris Fashion Week, Haute Couture).
• Birthplace of Impressionism (Monet, Renoir, Degas).
• Vibrant theater scene: Opéra Garnier, Comédie‑Française. | | **Cuisine** | • Classic French dishes: croissants, baguettes, escargot, coq au vin.
• Michelin‑starred restaurants (e.g., Le Cinq, L’Arpège).
• Café culture: sidewalk cafés, patisseries, and brasseries. | | **Transportation** | • Extensive metro network (16 lines, ~300 km).
• RER commuter trains connect suburbs.
• Bicycle-sharing system (Vélib’). | | **Economy** | • Major global financial hub; headquarters of many multinational corporations.
• Strong tourism sector: ~30 million visitors annually pre‑COVID. | | **Education & Research** | • Home to prestigious universities: Sorbonne, Sciences Po, École Normale Supérieure.
• Leading research institutions in physics, mathematics, and humanities. | If you’d like more specific details—such as travel tips, historical anecdotes, culinary recommendations, or current events—just let me know!
